judged_text: createEvent now selects the target calendar solely via find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId) with a 'primary' fallback, dropping the old destinationCalendar.externalId selection, so destination rows with a null credentialId never match. Users with pre-refactor DestinationCalendar rows (null credentialId) get events created on their primary calendar instead of the calendar they selected, and the EventManager fallback branch then creates one event on the primary of every matching same-provider credential, producing duplicate calendar events where the old code produced one.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, the target calendar is now selected via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` with a fallback to `"primary"` (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). If a `DestinationCalendar` entry has `credentialId` null/undefined (pre-refactor rows), it will never match and will fall back to primary, ignoring the intended `externalId`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when `destination.credentialId` is missing it loops all credentials of the same integration (`filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)`) and calls `createEvent(c, event)` for each; previously, non-owning credentials would likely fail via 404 when inserting into the selected `externalId`, but now all can succeed on their own `primary`, creating duplicate events. This matches the finding and is verifiable from the diff.
